column1: # boru Language Specification: within-type scalar & Micron operations
# Every scalar type and every Micron kind has WELL-DEFINED behaviour under
# the binary arithmetic words add / sub / mul / div / mod / pow, applied
# WITHIN a type (never across it — a cross-type pair is a type error).
# Rows use the infix form `a op b`, which reads naturally (the handler
# computes `a OP b`); the pure forward form `op a b` reverses the operands,
# exactly like the numeric words (see arithmetic.tsv).
#   sub : remove every occurrence of the right operand
#   mod : the tail after the LAST occurrence (whole string if none)
#   pow : the left operand repeated once per character of the right

column3: sub with no occurrence is unchanged
div with no occurrence is zero
mod is the tail after the last separator
mod with no occurrence is the whole string
mul is the Cartesian character product
pow repeats the left once per right char
pow by an empty string is empty
sub by an empty string is unchanged

column1: # §5  Micron — the field-wise default over the primary field map
# Emailon: user and host concatenate field-wise, rebuilt via `make`.
# Coloron: numeric channels add; a channel that leaves 0..255 is a loud make error.

column3: Coloron add overflow errors via the validator

column1: # Semveron: numeric components add; string components concatenate.
# user kind: field-wise default over the schema, rendered as its field map.
def Pointon refine Micron {x:Integer y:Integer} (make Pointon {x:1 y:2}) add (make Pointon {x:10 y:20})
column3: user Micron add uses the field-wise default

column1: def Pointon refine Micron {x:Integer y:Integer} (make Pointon {x:5 y:9}) sub (make Pointon {x:2 y:3})
# cross-kind is an error (within a kind, not across).
# §6  Micron — user overrides win over the default
# A more specific [Kindon Kindon] signature the user adds REPLACES the
def Pointon refine Micron {x:Integer y:Integer} def add fn [[a:Pointon b:Pointon] [Integer] [(a.x add b.x) add (a.y add b.y)]] (make Pointon {x:1 y:2}) add (make Pointon {x:10 y:20})
column3: a user override replaces the field-wise default

Pathon sub with no matching suffix is unchanged
